question: On a multi-lane roadway posted at 35 mph, may the single-lane regulatory-sign size be used, and what size must a STOP sign still use?
model_answer: Direct Answer: No. On a 35-mph roadway the reduced ("Minimum") sizes may not be used, because the MUTCD restricts sizes smaller than the Conventional Road sizes to low-speed facilities with operating speeds of 30 mph or less; at 35 mph the full Conventional Road (or larger) sizes govern. However, the evidence provided does not include the regulatory sign size table for the STOP sign (R1-1) itself, so I cannot state the exact required STOP sign dimensions for this situation from this evidence. Standards (mandatory): - "The sign dimensions prescribed in the sign size tables in the various Parts and Chapters in this Manual and in the 'Standard Highway Signs' publication (see Section 1A.05) shall be used unless engineering judgment determines that other sizes are appropriate in accordance with the following." - "The sizes shown in the Minimum columns that are smaller than the sizes shown in the Conventional Road columns in the various sign size tables in this Manual shall only be used on low-speed roadways, alleys, site roadways open to public travel, and on low-volume rural roads with operating speeds of 30 mph or less; and only where the reduced legend size would be adequate for the regulation or warning or where physical conditions preclude the use of larger sizes." — A posted 35-mph multi-lane roadway does not meet this condition, so the smaller sizes shall not be used. Guidance (recommended): - For school-area regulatory signs, "The sizes in the Oversized column should be used on roadways that have four or more lanes with posted speed limits of 40 mph or higher" (not triggered at 35 mph, where Conventional Road sizes apply). Visual evidence: - [Image 1] Table 2D-2 (Sheet 1, Post-Mounted Signs) distinguishes Single-Lane and Multi-Lane letter/numeral sizes for guide signs by speed range (e.g., 30–40 mph columns), showing that multi-lane roads generally require larger legend sizes than single-lane roads at the same speed. - [Image 2] Table 7B-1 lists Conventional Road, Minimum, and Oversized sizes for school-area signs and plaques, and its note states that minimum sign sizes for multi-lane conventional roads shall be as shown in the Conventional Road column — reinforcing that reduced sizes are not for multi-lane roads. - [Image 5] shows the Section 2A.07 Standard text restricting Minimum-column sizes to low-speed roadways with operating speeds of 30 mph or less. - [Image 3], [Image 4], [Image 6], [Image 7], and [Image 8] do not provide the regulatory-sign size table (e.g., R1-1 dimensions) needed to state the exact STOP sign size. Citations: - Section 2A.07 Standard §2 (p.45) - Section 7B.01 Guidance §3 (p.972) - Section 2D.07 Guidance §5 (p.210) - Table 2D-2 (p.210) - Table 7B-1 (p.971)
gold_answer: For regulatory signs other than STOP, the single-lane size may be used at 35 mph or less. The STOP-sign exception remains: the multi-lane STOP size is 36 x 36 inches.
